fields.reasoning: The intent (change set 01M6XMT, part 2) asks that land/fold accept a log where a later op's base was superseded only by its own change set's earlier op, so 01M6WMCCRC0K lands as written. model.checkBase (internal/model/apply.go:284) is the one place every node and link op's base is checked, and history entries already carry their ChangeSet, so a same-change-set skip there is a small, uniform change. Limiting it to node.retire would leave the same trap for link retires and for update-after-update written on an old base by a parallel session in one change set, where the ops are one unit of intent and cannot conflict with themselves in any meaningful sense. Conflict detection between change sets, which is what the stale-base check protects, is untouched.
fields.statement: Apply the rule to every op type on nodes and links, checked in model.checkBase: when walking the target's history after an op's base, skip entries written by the op's own change set, so an op is never stale against its own change set's ops. Entries from other change sets after the base still conflict on overlapping aspects exactly as today, including ones interleaved between the change set's own ops. The other checks are unchanged: a base that is not an operation on the target still fails, and writing a retired target still fails.
